images.caption: Figure 1:ID-Forcing extends autoregressive video generation far beyond the training horizon.In-distribution KV operations suppress color and motion drift, enabling stable minute-scale generation.

Figure 2:Same conditioning, different provenance.We generate the next chunkx7x_{7}from the same conditioning windowκ1:6\kappa_{1:6}, varying only how the last chunk of the horizon,x6x_{6}, is cached intoκ6\kappa_{6}.Case 1(self-caching):x6x_{6}attends to no prior entry, andx7x_{7}shows no drifting.Case 2(self-forcing caching):x6x_{6}attends to a window never seen in training, andx7x_{7}degrades.Case 3(sink caching): keeping the first chunk does not help, as the window is still unseen in training.
Thus, how a chunk is cached alone can determine whether the next chunk drifts.
Figure 4:Qualitative comparison on 2-minute videos.Full videos are available at thislink.

Figure 5:Qualitative ablation on 2-minute video.Components are added from top to bottom. Without self-caching, colors and textures still drift even with the sink and re-rotation, whereas the full ID-Forcing preserves the scene and color throughout the 2-minute video.
